The Blazor Web App is ready. Here's what was built:

**Architecture:** Blazor **Auto** render mode — pages load instantly via Server-side rendering on first visit, then switch to **WebAssembly** for snappy client-side interactivity (no server round-trips after WASM loads).

**Key files created/modified:**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Client/Models/ShipmentDto.cs` | Shared shipment model + status enum |
| `Client/Services/ShipmentService.cs` | HTTP client for API calls (works in both Server & WASM) |
| `Client/Pages/Dispatcher.razor` | Sortable/filterable dashboard with inline status updates |
| `Client/Pages/TrackShipment.razor` | Customer tracking with progress visualization |
| `Data/Shipment.cs` | EF Core entity |
| `Data/ApplicationDbContext.cs` | DB context with seed data (8 shipments) + role seeding |
| `Endpoints/ShipmentEndpoints.cs` | Minimal API endpoints with role-based auth |
| `Program.cs` | Identity with roles, auto-migration, endpoint mapping |

**Auth:** ASP.NET Core Identity with **Dispatcher** and **Customer** roles. Dispatcher dashboard requires the `Dispatcher` role; tracking page requires any authenticated user.

Run with: `cd ShipmentTracker/ShipmentTracker && dotnet run`
